text: Invoices don't always arrive clean, and problems don't always surface on the first validation pass. Sometimes a distribution needs a different account, or a hold reveals a genuine data error rather than a real dispute. This lesson covers adjusting an invoice after it's saved - and where that stops being simple.

A validated invoice isn't permanently locked. You can still edit distributions, correct a line amount, fix an account combination. But doing so knocks the status back to Needs Revalidation - Fusion requires it to be re-checked by Validate before it can proceed, because an edited invoice is, by definition, no longer the exact invoice that was originally validated.

How much you can edit narrows as the invoice progresses. Validated but not yet accounted is the most flexible state - most fields stay editable, and editing just triggers revalidation. Accounted but not yet paid is more constrained - posted distributions generally shouldn't be silently altered. Paid or partially paid is the hard stop - Payables normally blocks updating or reversing distributions there, because the payment itself was built from the invoice's accounting at that exact moment.

That progression makes sense once you see what depends on the invoice looking the way it did. A validated-but-unaccounted invoice has only affected Payables itself. An accounted invoice has posted journal entries other reports may reference. A paid invoice has generated an actual outbound payment tied to specific amounts - changing it after the fact would disconnect it from what already happened.

Take an invoice from Maple and Co. Printing, miscoded to the wrong cost center but caught before accounting - a simple distribution fix and a revalidation clears it. Caught only after payment, that same fix needs a different mechanism entirely, which is exactly what the next lesson covers. Up next, lesson twenty-two, the final lesson of Chapter 4: cancelling and reversing invoices.
